chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the wealth that is not put to work and is not circulated, and he said: 'Zakat is obligatory upon it every year, unless it is minted (coinage).'
ai.seo_question: What is the zakat ruling for wealth that is not circulated or put to work?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that wealth held in reserve without being circulated or invested (stagnant) is subject to annual zakat, provided it has not been minted into standard coinage (dinar/dirham). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuous growth of capital as a trigger for zakat liability, distinguishing between raw bullion and circulating currency. It underscores the principle that wealth accumulates religious dues even when idle, reinforcing the social welfare function of zakat.
